Test Scenario: Register with valid details
Preconditions: User is on the Sign Up page; email not yet registered.
Test Steps:
1. Open the Sign Up page
2. Enter full name, valid email and a valid password
3. Submit the form
Test Data:
Name: Juan Dela Cruz
Email: juan.test01@mail.com
Password: Test@1234
Expected Result: Account is created and stored in Supabase; user is told to verify email / is directed to Login. No error is shown.

Test Scenario: Register with an already-registered email
Test Steps:
1. Open Sign Up
2. Enter the existing email with any valid password
3. Submit
Expected Result: Registration is rejected with a clear 'email already registered' message; no duplicate account is created.

Test Scenario: Register with invalid email format
Test Steps:
1. Enter an email without '@' or domain
2. Fill other fields validly
3. Submit
Expected Result: Validation message is shown; form is not submitted.

Test Scenario: Register with required fields left blank
Test Steps:
1. Leave one or more required fields empty
2. Submit
Expected Result: Each missing required field is flagged; no account is created.

Test Scenario: Register with weak / too-short password
Test Steps:
1. Enter valid name and email
2. Enter a password that violates the password policy
3. Submit
Expected Result: Registration is rejected and the password requirement is displayed. (Confirm the exact policy with the Backend developer.)

Test Scenario: Login with valid credentials
Test Steps:
1. Open Login page
2. Enter registered email and password
3. Click Login
Expected Result: User is authenticated and redirected to the User Dashboard.

Test Scenario: Login with wrong password
Test Steps:
1. Enter registered email with an incorrect password
2. Click Login
Expected Result: Login is denied with an error message; no session is created; message does not reveal which field was wrong.

Test Scenario: Login with unregistered email
Preconditions: Email is not in the system.
Test Steps:
1. Enter an unregistered email and any password
2. Click Login
Expected Result: Login is denied with an error message; no dashboard access.

Test Scenario: Login with blank fields
Test Steps:
1. Leave email and/or password blank
2. Click Login
Expected Result: Validation messages are displayed; no request succeeds.

Test Scenario: Unverified account cannot post or claim food
Preconditions: Account registered but email not verified.
Test Steps:
1. Try to log in with the unverified account
2. If login is allowed, try to post food and claim food
Expected Result: User is blocked from logging in or from posting/claiming until the account is verified.

Test Scenario: Logout ends the session
Test Steps:
1. Click Logout
2. Press the browser Back button
3. Try to open the dashboard URL directly
Expected Result: Session is ended; protected pages redirect to Login.

Test Scenario: Password is not stored in plain text
Test Steps:
1. Open the Supabase auth user record for the test account
2. Inspect the stored password field
Expected Result: Only a hashed password is stored; the plain password is not visible anywhere in the database or in network responses.

Test Scenario: Admin login with valid credentials
Test Steps:
1. Open Admin Login
2. Enter admin email and password
3. Click Login
Expected Result: Admin is authenticated and redirected to the Admin Dashboard.

Test Scenario: Admin login with invalid credentials
Test Steps:
1. Enter wrong admin password
2. Click Login
Expected Result: Login is denied; no admin access is granted.

Test Scenario: Regular user cannot log in to Admin side
Test Steps:
1. Open Admin Login
2. Enter the regular user's credentials
Expected Result: Access is denied; user is not shown the Admin Dashboard.

Test Scenario: Dashboard shows Find Food and Donate Food options
Test Steps:
1. Log in as a regular user
2. Observe the User Dashboard
Expected Result: Dashboard loads and clearly presents both 'Find Food' and 'Donate Food' options.

Test Scenario: Find Food option opens available food list
Test Steps: 1. Click 'Find Food'
Expected Result: Available Food list page is displayed.

Test Scenario: Donate Food option opens the food posting form
Test Steps: 1. Click 'Donate Food'
Expected Result: Post Food form is displayed.

Test Scenario: Same account can both post and claim food
Preconditions: User A is logged in; User B has an available post.
Test Steps:
1. As User A, post a food item
2. As User A, claim User B's food
Expected Result: Both actions succeed with the same account without switching roles.

Test Scenario: Unauthenticated user cannot open the dashboard
Test Steps: 1. Paste the User Dashboard URL into the browser
Expected Result: User is redirected to Login; no dashboard data is shown.

Test Scenario: Browse available food posts
Preconditions: At least 3 published posts with remaining quantity exist from other users.
Test Steps:
1. Log in
2. Click Find Food
Expected Result: All available posts are listed with key info (name, category, quantity, expiry, location).

Test Scenario: View complete food details
Test Steps: 1. From the list, click a food post
Expected Result: Details page shows name, description, category, remaining quantity, unit, expiration date/time, pickup location and instructions, and donor.

Test Scenario: Expired posts are not shown as available
Preconditions: A post whose expiration date/time has passed exists.
Test Steps:
1. Open Find Food
2. Look for the expired post
Expected Result: Expired post is not listed as available (or is clearly marked and cannot be claimed).

Test Scenario: Posts with zero remaining quantity are not available
Preconditions: A post with 0 remaining quantity exists.
Test Steps:
1. Open Find Food
2. Look for the fully-claimed post
Expected Result: Post is not listed as available for claiming.

Test Scenario: Empty state when no food is available
Test Steps: 1. Open Find Food
Expected Result: A friendly 'no food available' message is shown; no errors or blank broken layout.

Test Scenario: Claim available food with valid quantity
Preconditions: User B logged in; User A's post has 10 portions remaining.
Test Steps:
1. Open the post details
2. Enter a quantity within the remaining amount
3. Click Claim
Expected Result: Claim is created and a confirmation is displayed (Claim Confirmation screen).

Test Scenario: Remaining quantity updates after claim
Test Steps:
1. Re-open the post details
2. Check remaining quantity in Find Food and in Supabase
Expected Result: Remaining quantity decreased by the claimed amount in the UI and the database.

Test Scenario: User cannot claim their own food post
Preconditions: User A has a published post.
Test Steps:
1. Log in as User A
2. Open own post in Find Food (if listed)
3. Try to claim it; also attempt via direct URL / API call
Expected Result: Claim is blocked (button hidden/disabled or error shown) and no claim record is created.

Test Scenario: Claim quantity greater than remaining is rejected
Test Steps:
1. Open the post
2. Enter a quantity above the remaining amount
3. Click Claim
Expected Result: Claim is rejected with an error; remaining quantity unchanged.

Test Scenario: Claim exactly the remaining quantity
Test Steps: 1. Claim exactly the remaining quantity
Expected Result: Claim succeeds; remaining quantity becomes 0 and the post is no longer available to others.

Test Scenario: Invalid claim quantities are rejected
Test Steps:
1. Try to claim with 0
2. Try a negative number
3. Try non-numeric text
4. Try an empty value
Expected Result: Each invalid value is rejected with a validation message; no claim is created.

Test Scenario: Cannot claim a post that expired
Preconditions: A post expires while its details page is open.
Test Steps:
1. Open the post before expiry
2. Wait until after the expiry time
3. Click Claim
Expected Result: Claim is rejected because the post is expired; no claim is created.

Test Scenario: Stale page claim after post becomes unavailable
Preconditions: User B has a post page open; User C claims all remaining quantity.
Test Steps:
1. User C claims the full remaining quantity
2. User B (stale page) tries to claim
Expected Result: User B's claim is rejected with a message; no over-claim occurs.

Test Scenario: Claim confirmation shows claim details
Test Steps: 1. Review the Claim Confirmation screen
Expected Result: Confirmation displays food name, quantity claimed, and pickup details; the claim appears in My Claims.

Test Scenario: View pickup information for a claimed food
Test Steps:
1. Open My Claims
2. Open the claim
Expected Result: Pickup location, instructions, and donor details are displayed.

Test Scenario: View claim status in My Claims
Preconditions: User has claims in different states.
Test Steps:
1. Open My Claims
2. Check the status shown for each claim
Test Data: Claims in Pending, Ready for Pickup, Picked Up, Completed
Expected Result: Each claim shows its correct status and only the user's own claims are listed.

Test Scenario: Cancel a claim
Preconditions: User has an active claim not yet picked up.
Test Steps:
1. Open My Claims
2. Cancel the claim
3. Check the post's remaining quantity
Expected Result: Claim status becomes Cancelled. Verify with the team whether quantity is returned to the post (rule not defined in BRD).

Test Scenario: Claimer cannot change the pickup status of the donor's post
Preconditions: User B has a claim on User A's post.
Test Steps: 1. As User B, try to set status to Picked Up/Completed via UI or direct request
Expected Result: Action is not available or is rejected; only the donor can update pickup status. (See BRD note: BR-10 vs BRU-09.)

Test Scenario: Post food with all valid details
Test Steps:
1. Click Donate Food
2. Fill in all fields
3. Submit the form
Test Data:
Name: Pandesal
Description: Freshly baked
Category: Bakery
Qty: 20 pcs
Expiry: tomorrow 6:00 PM
Pickup: Brgy. Hall
Instructions: Ask for Ana
Expected Result: Post is saved with all entered details.

Test Scenario: Publish a food post
Test Steps:
1. Click Publish
2. Log in as another user
3. Open Find Food
Expected Result: Post becomes Available and is visible to other users.

Test Scenario: Required fields blank when posting
Test Steps:
1. Leave required fields empty (name, category, quantity, expiry, pickup location)
2. Submit
Expected Result: Validation messages appear per field; post is not created or published.

Test Scenario: Expiration date/time in the past is rejected
Test Steps:
1. Enter an expiration earlier than the current date/time
2. Submit
Expected Result: Post is rejected with an error about the expiration.

Test Scenario: Invalid quantity values are rejected
Test Steps:
1. Enter 0, a negative number, and text in Quantity
2. Submit each
Expected Result: Each invalid value is rejected with a validation message.

Test Scenario: Category dropdown lists admin-managed categories
Test Steps:
1. Open the Post Food form
2. Open the Category field
Expected Result: All active categories created by the admin are selectable.

Test Scenario: Pickup location and instructions are shown to claimers
Preconditions: A published post with pickup details exists.
Test Steps: 1. As another user, open the post details
Expected Result: Pickup location and instructions match what the donor entered.

Test Scenario: New published post starts as Available
Test Steps: 1. Open My Donations
Expected Result: The post shows status 'Available'.

Test Scenario: Special characters / script input is handled safely
Test Steps:
1. Enter <script>alert(1)</script> in name and description
2. Publish and view the post as another user
Expected Result: Input is saved/escaped safely; no script runs; page does not break.

Test Scenario: My Donations lists only the user's own posts with status
Test Steps: 1. Open My Donations
Expected Result: Only the user's own posts are shown with correct statuses (Available, Claimed, Picked Up, Completed).

Test Scenario: Edit own food post
Preconditions: User has an Available post with no claims.
Test Steps:
1. Open the post in My Donations
2. Edit quantity/description
3. Save
Expected Result: Changes are saved and reflected in Find Food.

Test Scenario: Remove / cancel own food post
Test Steps:
1. Open My Donations
2. Remove or cancel the post
Expected Result: Post is no longer available to claimers; record is handled per system design.

Test Scenario: Post status changes when someone claims
Test Steps:
1. Another user claims the post
2. Refresh My Donations
Expected Result: Status updates to claimed and the claim appears with the claimer's details.

Test Scenario: Donor sets status to Ready for Pickup
Test Steps:
1. Open My Donations
2. Update status to Ready for Pickup
Expected Result: Status changes to Ready for Pickup and the claimer sees the same status.

Test Scenario: Donor sets Picked Up then Completed
Test Steps:
1. Update status to Picked Up
2. Update status to Completed
Expected Result: Statuses update in order; the claim becomes Completed.

Test Scenario: Completed transaction is recorded as Food Rescued
Test Steps:
1. Check My Donations / My Claims
2. Check the transaction record in Supabase
Expected Result: Completed transaction is retained and labeled as Food Rescued; not deleted.

Test Scenario: Status cannot skip steps or go backward
Test Steps:
1. Try to set Available straight to Completed
2. Try to move a Completed post back
Expected Result: Invalid transitions are blocked.

Test Scenario: Non-owner cannot update another user's post status
Preconditions: User B knows the post ID of User A's post.
Test Steps: 1. As User B, send a status update for User A's post (UI/URL/Postman)
Expected Result: Request is rejected (not authorized); status is unchanged.

Test Scenario: Users cannot see another user's claims
Test Steps:
1. As User A open My Claims
2. Try opening User B's claim by URL/ID
Expected Result: Only own claims are visible; other user's data is not accessible.

Test Scenario: View user profile
Test Steps: 1. Open Profile
Expected Result: Profile shows the user's registered details.

Test Scenario: Update profile information
Test Steps:
1. Edit name/contact
2. Save
3. Reload page
Expected Result: Updates are saved and persist after reload; invalid input is rejected.

Test Scenario: Admin dashboard displays system statistics

Expected Result: Dashboard shows monitoring info and statistics (e.g., users, food posts, claims, rescued).

Test Scenario: Dashboard figures match the database

Expected Result: All numbers match the stored data.

Test Scenario: Dashboard navigation to modules works

Expected Result: Each link opens the correct Admin module without errors.

Test Scenario: Regular user cannot open Admin pages by URL

Expected Result: Access is denied or redirected; no admin data is shown.

Test Scenario: View list of users

Test Scenario: Search for a user

Test Scenario: Only admins can manage users (API level)

Test Scenario: View all food posts and statuses

Test Scenario: Filter / search food posts by status

Test Scenario: View all claims and statuses

Test Steps:

Expected Result: New claim appears with correct data and status.

Test Scenario: Filter / search claims

Expected Result: Results match the criteria.

Test Scenario: Regular user cannot manage categories

Test Scenario: View reports and statistics
Test Steps: 1. Open Reports & Statistics
Expected Result: Reports show totals for posts, claims, and completed (Food Rescued) transactions.

Test Scenario: Report figures are accurate

Expected Result: Report figures match the data exactly.

Test Scenario: Completed transactions are counted as Food Rescued

Test Scenario: Report with no data
Test Steps: 1. Open Reports

Test Scenario: Response time of standard actions
Test Steps:

Test Scenario: System availability during test period
Test Steps:

Expected Result: Tester completes posting without assistance.

Test Scenario: First-time user can claim food unaided
Preconditions: A tester who has never used FRSS.
Test Steps:
1. Ask tester to find and claim food without help
2. Observe
Expected Result: Tester completes claim without assistance.

Test Scenario: Responsive layout at 360px width
Test Steps:

2. Walk through key pages
Expected Result: All pages are readable and usable; no horizontal scrolling or overlapping.

Test Scenario: Layout on tablet and desktop
Test Steps: 1. Test at 768px and 1366px widths
Expected Result: Layouts adapt properly and remain readable.

Test Scenario: Works on Chrome, Firefox and Edge
Test Steps: 1. Run the core flow (login, post, claim) in each browser
Expected Result: Core flow works identically in all three browsers.

Test Scenario: Food post creation is logged
Test Steps:
1. Create a post
2. Check the Supabase record
Expected Result: Record has the user, timestamp, and action.

Test Scenario: Claims and status changes are logged
Test Steps:
1. Claim food
2. Change pickup status
3. Check records
Expected Result: Each event is recorded with user, timestamp, and action; 100% traceable.

Test Scenario: Role-based access enforced at API level
Test Steps: 1. Call admin endpoints using a regular user's token (Postman)
Expected Result: Calls are rejected; data isn't returned.

Test Scenario: User can't read other users' personal data
Test Steps: 1. As User A, request User B's profile data (Postman)
Expected Result: Request is rejected / returns no personal data.

Test Scenario: Injection resistance on inputs
Test Steps: 1. Enter SQL/JS payloads in text fields (login, post form, search)
Expected Result: Input is handled safely; no data leak or error.

Test Scenario: Large dataset performance
Test Steps:
1. Open Find Food and Admin lists

Test Scenario: Full flow: donate, claim, pickup, complete
Preconditions: Two user accounts and an admin.
Test Steps:
1. Donor registers/logs in and posts then publishes food
2. Claimer finds and claims it
3. Donor sets Ready for Pickup, Picked Up, Completed
4. Admin checks the claim and report
Expected Result: Every step succeeds, statuses stay in sync for both users, and the transaction is recorded as Food Rescued and visible to Admin.

Test Scenario: Claim updates user and admin views
Test Steps:
1. Claim food
2. Check My Claims, donor's My Donations, Admin Food and Claims monitoring
Expected Result: Quantity and status are consistent in all four places.

Test Scenario: Multiple partial claims until quantity is zero
Test Steps:
1. User B claims 4
2. User C claims 4
3. User D claims 2
4. User E tries to claim
Expected Result: Each claim reduces quantity; after the third, post is unavailable and User E is blocked.

Test Scenario: Two users claim the last portions at the same time
Test Steps:
1. Both users open the post
2. Both click Claim at the same time
Expected Result: Only one claim succeeds; the other gets an error; quantity never goes below 0.

Test Scenario: Post becomes unavailable after expiry
Test Steps:
1. Wait for expiry
2. Check Find Food and try to claim
Expected Result: Post is no longer available; claim is blocked.

Test Scenario: Category rename reflects on existing posts
Test Steps:
1. Admin renames category
2. Check posts in Find Food and Admin Food Monitoring
Expected Result: Updated category name appears consistently.

Test Scenario: Completed records stay after later activity
Test Steps:
1. Perform new posts/claims
2. Check history and reports
Expected Result: Completed records are retained and still included in reports.
